answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy means making each identity cost real resources. One mechanism: a per-agent bond in an opal-denominated escrow, slashed when identities share a controller. Registration locks the bond plus a pay-per-identity fee, and the protocol keeps an atlas of funding-graph edges linking wallets, IP ranges and payment rails. When a cluster traces to one funding source, every bond in it is forfeited. Farming N identities forces the attacker to post N bonds and lose them all, so cost grows linearly while yield collapses. Honest agents hold the bond as a haven of trust.
